articles.title: Sự thống nhất giữa Đạo đức, Khoa học và Nghệ thuật
articles.text:
Thế giới hôm nay đang bước vào kỷ nguyên AI, dữ liệu lớn và tự động hóa. Chưa bao giờ con người có nhiều công cụ khoa học đến vậy. Đồng thời, những tổ chức thành công cũng ngày càng chú trọng đến khả năng truyền cảm hứng, dẫn dắt thay đổi và xây dựng văn hóa – những biểu hiện của nghệ thuật quản trị.
Nhưng cũng chính trong thời đại ấy, chúng ta chứng kiến không ít doanh nghiệp sụp đổ, không phải vì thiếu tri thức hay thiếu tài năng, mà vì thiếu đạo đức. Có những tổ chức sở hữu công nghệ hàng đầu, hệ thống quản trị hiện đại và đội ngũ lãnh đạo xuất sắc, nhưng vẫn đánh mất niềm tin của xã hội vì gian dối, vì đặt lợi ích ngắn hạn lên trên lợi ích lâu dài, hoặc vì coi con người chỉ là phương tiện.
Điều đó cho thấy, lãnh đạo, quản trị và quản lý không chỉ là câu chuyện của khoa học và nghệ thuật. Chúng phải được xây dựng trên một nền tảng cao hơn: đạo đức.
Theo cách nhìn đó, Lãnh đạo, Quản trị và Quản lý là sự thống nhất giữa Đạo đức, Khoa học và Nghệ thuật.
Đạo đức là gốc
Đạo đức trả lời câu hỏi quan trọng nhất: Ta làm việc này vì điều gì?
Một nhà lãnh đạo có thể rất thông minh, nhưng nếu thiếu đạo đức, trí tuệ ấy có thể bị sử dụng sai mục đích.
Một nhà quản lý có thể rất giỏi tối ưu hiệu quả, nhưng nếu chỉ chạy theo lợi nhuận mà bỏ qua con người, hiệu quả ấy sẽ không bền vững.
Đạo đức không chỉ là sự trung thực hay liêm chính. Đạo đức trong quản trị doanh nghiệp còn là trách nhiệm với khách hàng, với người lao động, với cổ đông, với cộng đồng và với các thế hệ tương lai.
Đạo đức giúp người lãnh đạo biết rằng có những việc làm được nhưng không nên làm.
Có những cơ hội mang lại lợi nhuận rất lớn nhưng làm tổn hại xã hội. Có những quyết định giúp doanh nghiệp thắng trong ngắn hạn nhưng đánh mất niềm tin trong dài hạn.
Chính đạo đức tạo ra giới hạn để quyền lực không trở thành lạm quyền, tài năng không trở thành công cụ thao túng và công nghệ không trở thành mối đe dọa.
Đạo đức vì thế không phải là phần bổ sung của quản trị. Đó là nền móng của mọi quyết định.
Khoa học là nền
Nếu đạo đức cho chúng ta biết nên đi về đâu, thì khoa học giúp chúng ta biết đi bằng cách nào.
Khoa học quản trị là những tri thức có thể nghiên cứu, kiểm chứng, truyền dạy và không ngừng hoàn thiện. Đó là chiến lược, tài chính, quản trị nhân sự, quản trị vận hành, quản trị rủi ro, dữ liệu, AI, các mô hình quản trị hiện đại và những phương pháp ra quyết định dựa trên bằng chứng.
Khoa học giúp giảm sự ngẫu nhiên. Giúp tổ chức hoạt động ổn định. Giúp kinh nghiệm của một cá nhân trở thành năng lực của cả tổ chức.
Một doanh nghiệp muốn phát triển từ vài chục người lên vài nghìn người không thể chỉ dựa vào sự nhiệt huyết của người sáng lập. Họ phải xây dựng hệ thống, quy trình, tiêu chuẩn và cơ chế vận hành. Đó là sức mạnh của khoa học.
Trong thời đại AI, vai trò của khoa học càng trở nên quan trọng. AI sẽ giúp phân tích dữ liệu nhanh hơn, dự báo chính xác hơn, tối ưu nguồn lực tốt hơn và hỗ trợ ra quyết định hiệu quả hơn. Nhưng AI không thể quyết định mục tiêu cuối cùng của tổ chức. Điều đó vẫn thuộc về con người.
Nghệ thuật là đỉnh cao
Nếu khoa học tạo ra năng lực, thì nghệ thuật tạo ra sức sống.
Nghệ thuật trong lãnh đạo, quản trị và quản lý là khả năng biến những điều đúng thành những điều được mọi người tự nguyện thực hiện.
Không có công thức nào để truyền cảm hứng. Không có KPI nào đo được niềm tin. Không có quy trình nào tạo ra lòng trung thành. Đó là nghệ thuật.
Nghệ thuật là khả năng lắng nghe. Là biết khi nào phải quyết đoán và khi nào phải nhường. Là khả năng đọc được tâm lý con người. Là sự tinh tế trong giao tiếp. Là khả năng kết nối những con người rất khác nhau thành một tập thể cùng hướng tới một mục tiêu.
Các tổ chức có thể có quy trình giống nhau, nhưng văn hóa khác nhau. Có thể có chiến lược giống nhau, nhưng tinh thần khác nhau.
Sự khác biệt ấy được tạo nên bởi nghệ thuật.
Ba yếu tố trong Lãnh đạo, Quản trị và Quản lý
Ba yếu tố Đạo đức, Khoa học và Nghệ thuật đều hiện diện trong cả Lãnh đạo, Quản trị và Quản lý, nhưng với vai trò khác nhau.
Trong lãnh đạo, đạo đức định hình sứ mệnh và những giá trị không thể đánh đổi; khoa học giúp nhận diện xu thế và xây dựng chiến lược; nghệ thuật giúp truyền cảm hứng để mọi người cùng bước về tương lai.
Trong quản trị, đạo đức tạo nên văn hóa và các nguyên tắc ứng xử; khoa học thiết kế hệ thống, cơ chế và phương thức vận hành; nghệ thuật tạo ra sự đồng thuận để hệ thống được thực thi một cách tự nhiên.
Trong quản lý, đạo đức bảo đảm sự công bằng và trách nhiệm; khoa học chuẩn hóa quy trình, đo lường kết quả và kiểm soát chất lượng; nghệ thuật khơi dậy động lực, phát triển con người và xây dựng tinh thần đội ngũ.
Chính sự kết hợp hài hòa này làm nên năng lực của một tổ chức.
Kỷ nguyên AI càng đòi hỏi đạo đức
AI sẽ làm cho phần khoa học của quản trị ngày càng mạnh hơn. Máy tính có thể phân tích nhanh hơn con người. AI có thể viết báo cáo, dự báo thị trường, tối ưu sản xuất và hỗ trợ ra quyết định. Nhưng điều đó không làm vai trò của con người giảm đi, mà làm thay đổi vai trò ấy.
Con người sẽ ngày càng phải tập trung vào những việc mà AI khó thay thế: xác lập giá trị, lựa chọn mục tiêu, truyền cảm hứng, xây dựng văn hóa và chịu trách nhiệm trước xã hội.
Nói cách khác, khi khoa học ngày càng mạnh, đạo đức và nghệ thuật càng trở nên quan trọng.
Đó cũng là lý do vì sao nhà lãnh đạo của tương lai không chỉ cần giỏi công nghệ, mà còn phải là người có bản lĩnh đạo đức và chiều sâu nhân văn.
Một tổ chức muốn đi xa cần ba trụ cột
Đạo đức để biết điều gì đáng theo đuổi. Khoa học để biết cách thực hiện hiệu quả. Nghệ thuật để quy tụ con người và biến mục tiêu thành hiện thực.
Nếu thiếu đạo đức, khoa học và nghệ thuật có thể bị sử dụng sai hướng. Nếu thiếu khoa học, đạo đức và khát vọng khó trở thành kết quả. Nếu thiếu nghệ thuật, những hệ thống đúng đắn cũng khó chạm tới trái tim con người.
Vì vậy, lãnh đạo, quản trị và quản lý không phải là sự lựa chọn giữa đạo đức, khoa học hay nghệ thuật. Đó là sự hòa quyện của cả ba. Đạo đức là gốc, Khoa học là nền, Nghệ thuật là đỉnh.
Khi ba yếu tố ấy thống nhất trong một con người và trong một tổ chức, chúng ta không chỉ tạo ra hiệu quả, mà còn tạo ra niềm tin, không chỉ tạo ra tăng trưởng, mà còn tạo ra phát triển bền vững, không chỉ xây dựng những doanh nghiệp thành công, mà còn góp phần xây dựng một xã hội tốt đẹp hơn.

articles.title: Lame-duck Congress might actually do something: speed up energy projects
articles.text:
A massive permitting bill that could help energy projects come online much quicker and potentially lower utility bills for Americans is advancing with bipartisan support. And while it could be a catalyst for lots of clean energy, it could also speed up polluting projects and limit oversight of new data centers.
Lame-duck Congress might actually do something: speed up energy projects
The Senate will vote to push through a giant — and controversial — permitting reform bill.
Lame-duck Congress might actually do something: speed up energy projects
The Senate will vote to push through a giant — and controversial — permitting reform bill.
With data centers demanding more electricity for AI, environmental advocates fear that developers could take advantage of the reforms to evade public scrutiny and rely more heavily on fossil fuels. The bill sacrifices caution for speed, limiting environmental reviews and preventing communities from stopping a project from moving forward by taking it to court.
“Whether it is permits to bulldoze wetlands, the fast-tracking of gas pipelines or general environmental review, with this legislation, data centers would not need to answer to the concerns of local communities,” Christy Goldfuss, executive director of the nonprofit Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC), says in an email to The Verge. “People would be shocked to realize their representatives are rushing such a consequential decision.”
The bill sacrifices caution for speed
The sea change in Congress following the midterm elections could put the bill in an even more precarious position, giving Democrats a better shot at pushing for their priorities in the bill and potentially triggering a fight with President Donald Trump. Should it come up for a vote during the current lame-duck session or get kicked to next year, the bill will test whether Democrats and Republicans can actually get something done to address some of the biggest issues voters carried with them to the polls: rising energy costs and data centers encroaching on their communities.
“They swung big with this bill. It’s a really good bipartisan compromise,” Xan Fishman, executive vice president of the Energy Program at the Bipartisan Policy Center, tells The Verge.
Four senators calling themselves the “four corners” — Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Mike Lee (R-UT), and Martin Heinrich (D-NM) — introduced the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) on September 30th. “If we can pass this bill, we will flood the grid with clean, affordable energy and make data centers start paying their fair share,” Whitehouse, a climate hawk, said in the press release.
The announcement simultaneously garnered support from climate and renewable energy groups, as well as fossil fuel interests. “Pass the frickin’ bill so we can start building things again,” the US Oil & Gas Association said in a statement.
The Senate could vote to move the bill forward as early as next week, teeing it up for potential passage before the end of the year, according to the Bipartisan Policy Center. Fishman expects President Trump will want to sign the bill if the current Republican-controlled Congress acts, adding in an email that the White House has been “very involved” in negotiations. Newly empowered Democrats, however, could decide to drag out debate on the bill until next year in order to make fewer concessions to Republicans.
“Sometimes, bureaucratic processes that are created with good intentions kind of spiral out of control.”
If it becomes law, the bill would limit the reach of bedrock laws (stemming back to the 1970s environmental movement) that protect water resources and endangered species and give the public an opportunity to weigh in on large projects that might impact public health. Over the years, however, reviews that once took months at most might take several years or even decades, according to the Bipartisan Policy Center. Fishman attributes the delays largely to lengthy legal battles. Now, agencies have to spend more time preparing for lawsuits as they consider permitting applications, Fishman says. That holds up development on all kinds of infrastructure projects, including cleaner energy alternatives to fossil fuels.
Fishman expects BAAJA to be very effective in amending outdated permitting rules that have become burdensome to projects across the board, even those that might ultimately have a net positive impact on the environment. “Sometimes, bureaucratic processes that are created with good intentions kind of spiral out of control,” he says. “You want to protect the environment, you want to protect people, but you want to get to a yes or no [on a permit application] in a reasonable amount of time and you don’t want to have this endless litigation cycle.”
The bill would set a 45-day deadline for a lead agency to issue a decision on a project after completing an environmental review under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). In many cases, NEPA review is the only opportunity for nearby residents to weigh in on large projects that involve the federal government. And it’s been a key tool for opponents to high-profile projects including the Dakota Access and Keystone XL pipelines. BAAJA narrows the scope of projects subject to NEPA, creating exclusions for transmission upgrades and certain pipeline expansions, to name a couple. Many projects receiving federal loans or grants or that have already been through a similar state environmental assessment would no longer trigger NEPA review.
The bill also sets a strict new 150-day limit for anyone to challenge a project in court over alleged violations of NEPA, the Clean Water Act, Endangered Species Act, or National Historic Preservation Act. And BAAJA strips away a court’s ability to halt a project altogether even if it finds that a federal agency violated NEPA; it would simply force the agency to correct any issues.
The Clean Water Act allows the Army Corps of Engineers to issue general permits to projects that discharge dredged material into US waters as long as they’re deemed as having “minimal adverse environmental effects.” BAAJA could make it easier for large projects including data centers to qualify for those permits.
Some environmental groups are concerned that those general permits would take away public participation requirements for individual projects, especially when it comes to data centers that use a lot of water. The proposals in BAAJA amount to “rubber-stamping permits under the Clean Water Act” and “blocking interference from States and Tribes,” according to the environmental organization Earthjustice Action.
“It will enable fast delivery of gas to fuel the data center build-out.”
They’re also concerned that BAAJA aligns with the Trump administration’s push to deregulate industry and weaken environmental protections in order to swiftly build out more data centers and fossil fuel infrastructure to power them. Data center energy demand has led to a surge of new gas projects in the US, and the bipartisan bill could help streamline reviews for new pipelines delivering fuel for data centers.
“One very big reason why passing BAAJA is such a high priority for the gas industry is it will enable fast delivery of gas to fuel the data center build-out,” Earthjustice Action President Abigail Dillen said in a Thursday blog. “BAAJA delivers a precision strike for developers of dirty data centers.”
Long pipeline delays slow data center development, according to energy research firm Wood Mackenzie. Permitting reform could benefit data center developers building out their own gas generation rather than relying solely on the grid, so-called “behind-the-meter” projects, by ending regulatory delays when it comes to connecting pipelines. Reforms would also speed grid-connected gas generation, Wood Mackenzie says in a recent news release.
“I don’t think we’re seeing it as this bill helping one type of technology over the other. I think it clears the way for all technologies to get onto the grid a little quicker,” Siddhant Warrier, research analyst for North American Power for Wood Mackenzie, tells The Verge.
Notably, the bill is supposed to protect bipartisan interests by preventing any single administration from attacking a particular project type — such as the Biden administration attempting to phase down oil and gas in the power sector or the Trump administration issuing stop work orders to wind farms. BAAJA aims to provide “project certainty” by barring federal agencies from canceling or suspending permits they’ve already approved in most cases. It even allows developers to take agencies to court for “disparate treatment” to sue for damages incurred from project delays.
“This part of the legislation could also lead to a slew of industry lawsuits that result in taxpayers paying billions of dollars to private industry,” the NRDC warns in its analysis of the bill. It could also prevent communities from challenging projects, including data centers, that wind up having unforeseen consequences for the environment and public health.
Despite those concerns, the NRDC and other advocacy groups are optimistic about the bill boosting renewable energy and enabling power grid upgrades needed to meet rising demand while keeping costs down.
BAAJA could shorten the time needed to build a new transmission line nearly in half — from 10 years or more to around five or six years, the NRDC estimates. Transmission lines that carry electricity across long distances — key to getting electrons to urban centers from far-flung solar and wind farms — are particularly tricky to build because of the patchwork of permitting processes they’re subject to across different jurisdictions.
Two separate reports project that the permitting bill would increase renewable energy capacity in the US and cut greenhouse gas emissions as a result. It also points to modest reductions in energy costs as a result of BAAJA passing compared to a baseline reflecting the status quo. The average annual cost of producing electricity would fall by as much as 7 percent by 2041, according to modeling by think tank Resources for the Future. Household electricity bills would lower by $50 to $78 per year by 2040, according to an analysis by research firm Rhodium Group. The White House put out its own analysis in October claiming that the average household could see their electricity bills fall by as much as $251 each year as a result of BAAJA.
One of the ways BAAJA aims to keep utility bills from rising is to force data center developers to pay more for transmission costs. Current law prevents utilities from charging them for costs stemming from both new builds and existing infrastructure, which inadvertently shifts costs to other customers to fill in the gap. The bipartisan bill mandates what’s called “and pricing” so that data centers and other large electricity customers would be on the hook to pay for both added and existing infrastructure.
The bill would also require utilities to disclose electricity sales to data centers. It would force large data center developers to make financial assurances to utilities before they break ground, as well as make them responsible for covering costs of new energy projects even if the data center shutters before the infrastructure is paid off.
Unfortunately, the bill may only solve part of the problem since utility rates reflect more than just transmission costs. Increasing electricity demand from the data center boom can still raise prices for fuel and gas turbines, for example. And the bill doesn’t address other issues that have sparked backlash against data centers, like noise and air pollution from generators on site.
Still, without permitting reform, gas and power prices would likely continue to climb as new energy projects keep hitting bottlenecks, according to Wood Mackenzie. Even environmental groups concerned about some of the provisions in BAAJA are holding out to see if Congress can amend the bill to strengthen environmental and consumer protections.
The bill has become a sort of Rorschach test for its backers, one expert speaking on background tells The Verge. They’re all optimistic that their energy source of choice, be it oil and gas or solar and wind, will ultimately come out on top — as long as it gets the green light to build.

articles.title: Giá xăng dầu hôm nay 6/11: Thế giới tăng, xăng trong nước về 21.000 đồng/lít
articles.text:
Giá dầu thế giới hôm nay
Giá dầu trên thị trường quốc tế trong phiên giao dịch 5/11 quay đầu tăng mạnh sau khi giảm liên tiếp từ đầu tuần.
Kết thúc phiên giao dịch 5/11, theo Reuters, giá dầu Brent tăng 3,88%, lên mức 98,29 USD/thùng. Còn giá dầu WTI tăng 2,72%, chốt phiên ở mức 90,52 USD/thùng.
Trong phiên giao dịch trước đó (4/11), giá của cả hai loại dầu tiêu chuẩn đều giảm hơn 8%, xuống mức thấp nhất kể từ ngày 31/8.
Đầu phiên giao dịch hôm nay (6/11), giá dầu WTI của Mỹ tiếp tục đi lên.
Theo dữ liệu từ Oilprice, vào lúc 6h25' ngày 6/11 (giờ Việt Nam), giá dầu Brent vẫn được niêm yết ở mức 98,29 USD/thùng. Trong khi giá dầu WTI được điều chỉnh lên mức 91,38 USD/thùng, tăng 0,95% so với phiên liền trước.
Giá dầu thế giới đảo chiều tăng mạnh trong phiên giao dịch 5/11, sau khi các vụ tấn công mới nhằm vào tàu chở dầu tại Trung Đông làm gia tăng lo ngại về nguy cơ gián đoạn nguồn cung năng lượng toàn cầu. Diễn biến này khiến giới đầu tư đánh giá lại triển vọng cuộc xung đột giữa Mỹ - Israel và Iran, đồng thời cân nhắc khả năng các bên tiến tới thỏa thuận ngoại giao nhằm chấm dứt chiến tranh.
Tình hình an ninh tại Trung Đông tiếp tục diễn biến phức tạp.
Ngày 5/11, Saudi Arabia đã cảnh báo về những nguy cơ tiềm ẩn tại Yanbu, trung tâm xuất khẩu dầu mỏ quan trọng bên bờ Biển Đỏ, khi lực lượng Houthi ở Yemen tiếp tục tiến hành các cuộc tấn công nhằm vào nước này.
Sau đó, lực lượng Houthi tuyên bố đã tấn công sân bay King Fahd tại thành phố Dammam của Saudi Arabia.
Cũng trong ngày 5/11, Lực lượng Vệ binh Cách mạng Hồi giáo Iran cho biết, hai tàu chở dầu và một tàu kéo đã bốc cháy trong hai vụ việc riêng biệt sau khi tìm cách di chuyển qua các tuyến đường mà Tehran coi là trái phép tại eo biển Hormuz.
Trước đó, giá dầu giảm sâu sau khi kết quả bầu cử giữa nhiệm kỳ tại Mỹ cho thấy đảng Dân chủ đã giành được những thắng lợi quan trọng, làm gia tăng kỳ vọng về khả năng chính quyền của Tổng thống Donald Trump chịu thêm sức ép chính trị để tìm kiếm giải pháp kết thúc xung đột với Iran.
Giới phân tích nhận định nếu căng thẳng hạ nhiệt, hoạt động vận chuyển dầu qua eo biển Hormuz có thể được khôi phục ổn định hơn, qua đó giảm nguy cơ gián đoạn nguồn cung và hạ nhiệt giá năng lượng toàn cầu.
Không chỉ tại Trung Đông, xung đột giữa Nga và Ukraine cũng tác động đến triển vọng nguồn cung năng lượng.
Ukraine đã tiến hành lại các cuộc tấn công nhằm vào các nhà máy lọc dầu của Nga. Việc này làm dấy lên lo ngại về khả năng xuất khẩu dầu diesel của Moscow theo thỏa thuận với Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump.
Giá xăng dầu trong nước hôm nay
Tại thị trường trong nước, liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính đã tiến hành điều chỉnh giá xăng dầu từ chiều qua (5/11).
Ở kỳ điều hành 5/11, giá bán của các mặt hàng xăng dầu phổ biến trên thị trường được điều chỉnh giảm so với kỳ trước.
Cụ thể, giá bán lẻ tối đa của xăng E5RON92 giảm từ 23.203 đồng/lít xuống 20.898 đồng/lít, tương ứng giảm 2.305 đồng/lít so với kỳ điều hành gần nhất.
Giá xăng E10RON95-III giảm 2.075 đồng/lít, từ 23.231 đồng/lít xuống còn 21.156 đồng/lít.
Tương tự, các mặt hàng dầu cũng được điều chỉnh giảm. Giá dầu diesel 0.05S hạ 180 đồng/lít, từ 28.876 đồng/lít xuống còn 28.696 đồng/lít. Còn giá dầu mazut 180CST 3.5S giảm 1.969 đồng/kg, từ 23.974 đồng/kg xuống còn 22.005 đồng/kg.
Dữ liệu từ Bộ Công Thương cho thấy, giá bán lẻ xăng dầu tại Việt Nam đang ở mức thấp hơn so với các nước có chung đường biên giới.
Giá bán xăng dầu của các nước lân cận Việt Nam tính đến ngày 5/11 như sau:
Giá xăng tại Thái Lan là 32.001 đồng/lít (Chính phủ trợ giá); ở Campuchia là 31.887 đồng/lít (Chính phủ trợ giá); tại Lào là 47.148 đồng/lít; ở Trung Quốc là 36.125 đồng/lít (Chính phủ khống chế giá); tại Việt Nam không cao hơn 21.156 đồng/lít.
Giá dầu tại Thái Lan là 33.333 đồng/lít (Chính phủ trợ giá); ở Campuchia là 35.676 đồng/lít; tại Lào là 40.344 đồng/lít; ở Trung Quốc là 33.032 đồng/lít (Chính phủ khống chế giá); tại Việt Nam không cao hơn 28.696 đồng/lít.

articles.title: Amazon's Alexa for Shopping agent will now take your orders by text
articles.text:
Amazon is rolling out texting for Alexa for Shopping, its AI shopping agent, starting with invited US customers. It can find products, place orders and track prices by text. Sponsored products can show up in its replies, free to advertisers for now.
Amazon is letting shoppers text its AI shopping agent, Alexa for Shopping, which can search for products, compare them and place orders for them, the company said on Friday. The feature is starting with a small group of invited US customers, with millions more to get access in the coming weeks.
Customers who opt in get a contact called “Alexa Shopping.” They can text a request, such as needing more dog food, or send a photo of a recipe or an outfit, and the agent texts back with options. It buys with the customer’s approval, or automatically when a price hits a target they set.
It can also track price drops, reorder past purchases and check on packages. Amazon says a conversation started by text will carry over to its app, website and Alexa devices.
“Now with Alexa for Shopping, your personal shopping agent is just a text away,” said Rajiv Mehta, Amazon’s vice president of conversational shopping.
The text thread is also a new place for ads. Sponsored products can appear among the options the agent sends, though Amazon is not charging advertisers yet, and purchases the agent completes on its own carry no ads, Digiday reported. Amazon made more than $68B from advertising in 2025.
Amazon launched Alexa for Shopping in May and says more than 400 million customers used it in the past year. In September, it blocked Meta’s Muse agent from shopping its site. Last week, chief executive Andy Jassy said he expects Alexa for Shopping to become the main agent people use to buy from Amazon.
Rivals are moving into messaging too. OpenAI added texting to Dot, its personal agent, last month, and DoorDash began taking orders by text in September, GeekWire reported.

articles.title: Meta’s Muse AI can create custom ‘spaces’ for the version of the app you need right now
articles.text:
Meta will now allow you to build customized, app-like experiences within Muse. The new feature, called “spaces,” allows its AI assistant to build things like a shopping hub, school dashboard, music tracker, trivia game, and more, which you can interact with directly in the Muse app.
Meta’s Muse AI can create custom ‘spaces’ for the version of the app you need right now
You can create things like a shopping hub, school dashboard, or music tracker directly within Muse.
Meta says you can create a new space by describing it. If you connect an outside app to Muse — like Gmail, Google Calendar, OpenTable, Notion, and others Muse works with — the AI assistant will continuously pull information from them, allowing it to update pricing, dates, and other information in your space in the background. You can also interact with elements inside your spaces by checking things off, adding notes, and making edits.
You can also change the placement of your spaces in the Muse app, too, as Meta lets you keep them in the sidebar, move them into your main tab, or schedule when you see them. “For example, keep your weekly planner up front during the workweek, then swap it for your weekend plans on Saturday,” Meta says.
Meta also announced that it’s bringing new “Active Memory” and “Active Focus” capabilities from its Muse Wonder AI model into the Muse app and its Meta AI chatbot. This will allow Muse to understand when past information becomes relevant during conversations, as well as make it better at working toward goals.
Meta is rolling out spaces to all Muse users. The company is also looking into ways to share your spaces with other users and collaborate with them.

articles.title: Vì sao người dân 3 nước giàu nhất lại ít chuộng vàng trang sức?
articles.text:
Không phải vì người dân không có tiền mà vì một chuẩn mực xã hội đã biến việc phô bày sự giàu có thành điều tối kỵ.
Thị trường trang sức phân hóa mạnh
Quy mô thị trường vàng trang sức Bắc Âu được đánh giá là khá nhỏ so với nhiều khu vực khác trên thế giới. Tuy nhiên, cần phân biệt thị trường vàng trang sức với toàn bộ ngành bán lẻ trang sức, đồng hồ và phụ kiện.
Theo dữ liệu của Research and Markets, năm 2024, doanh thu bán lẻ trang sức, đồng hồ và phụ kiện tại ba nước Scandinavia gồm Thụy Điển, Đan Mạch và Na Uy đạt khoảng 3,4 tỷ USD. Trong đó, riêng trang sức và đồng hồ chiếm 1,9 tỷ USD, tương đương 57,2%.
Để so sánh, theo số liệu của Hội đồng Vàng Thế giới (WGC), nhu cầu vàng trang sức toàn cầu năm 2025 là 1.542,3 tấn, trong đó riêng Ấn Độ tiêu thụ 430,5 tấn, trị giá khoảng 49 tỷ USD. Toàn bộ quy mô thị trường của khu vực Bắc Âu chưa bằng một mùa cưới ở Ấn Độ.
Mở rộng ra lĩnh vực bán lẻ trang sức, đồng hồ và phụ kiện, tổng doanh thu năm 2024 của 3 nước Scandinavia (Thụy Điển, Đan Mạch, Na Uy) đạt 3,4 tỷ USD, trong đó trang sức và đồng hồ chiếm 1,9 tỷ USD, tương đương 57,2%.
Thụy Điển chiếm tỷ trọng lớn nhất với 43,4%, tiếp đến là Đan Mạch với 29,4% và Na Uy với 27,2%. Đáng chú ý, doanh thu toàn ngành trong giai đoạn 2019-2024 chỉ tăng trưởng kép khoảng 0,1%, cho thấy thị trường gần như đi ngang.
Nhưng “quy mô nhỏ” và “không sinh lời” là 2 chuyện khác nhau. Đặc điểm đáng chú ý nhất của thị trường này là sự phân hóa bên trong.
Lấy Na Uy làm ví dụ, tờ báo kinh doanh E24 dẫn dữ liệu ngành cho thấy năm 2024, doanh số của các nhà kim hoàn ở phân khúc giá thấp nhất giảm 3%. Người tiêu dùng tìm mua trang sức dưới 10.000 NOK (khoảng 27,8 triệu đồng) rất nhạy cảm với giá vàng, khiến doanh số vàng ở phân khúc này sụt giảm rõ rệt.
Trong khi đó, tại David-Andersen - một trong những thương hiệu kim hoàn lâu đời nhất Na Uy, doanh số trang sức xa xỉ có giá trên 100.000 NOK (khoảng 278 triệu đồng) lại tăng ngược dòng 20%.
Một chiếc nhẫn có giá lên tới 2 triệu NOK (khoảng 5,5 tỷ đồng) đã được bán cho một khách hàng nữ ngoài 50 tuổi, mua cho chính mình và “hoàn toàn không bận tâm đến giá vàng”.
Sự phân hóa này gắn trực tiếp với diễn biến giá vàng. Năm 2024, vàng lập 40 kỷ lục giá mới và tiếp tục tăng trong năm 2025 với mức tăng 45% trong một năm.
Dữ liệu của WGC cho thấy sản lượng tiêu thụ trang sức vàng toàn cầu năm 2025 giảm xuống còn 1.542,3 tấn, giảm 18% so với cùng kỳ và là mức thấp nhất trong 5 năm; nhưng tổng giá trị tiêu thụ trang sức vàng toàn cầu trong cùng kỳ lại tăng 18%, đạt mức kỷ lục 172 tỷ USD.
Tại châu Âu, nhu cầu trang sức vàng cả năm ước khoảng 131 tấn, nhưng diễn biến theo quý phân hóa mạnh, sản lượng tiêu thụ quý II giảm 4% so với cùng kỳ, trong khi quý III lại tăng hơn 30%.
Cục diện “sản lượng giảm, giá trị tăng, phân hóa nội bộ” này chính là minh chứng ở tầm vĩ mô cho thực tế tại thị trường Bắc Âu: phân khúc bình dân thu hẹp, còn phân khúc siêu cao cấp vẫn vững vàng.
Thị trường này “nhỏ” không phải vì thiếu nhu cầu, mà vì tầng giữa - những người tiêu dùng vừa muốn chất liệu vàng, vừa nhạy cảm với giá đang bị đẩy ra ngoài một cách có hệ thống.
Khi giá vàng nguyên liệu vượt mốc 1.300 NOK (khoảng 3,6 triệu đồng) mỗi gram, chi phí đầu vào của trang sức phổ thông tăng theo, khiến nhóm khách hàng này ngày càng khó tiếp cận sản phẩm.
Luật Jante và văn hóa tiêu dùng kín đáo
Một yếu tố văn hóa thường được nhắc đến khi lý giải cách người Bắc Âu tiêu dùng hàng xa xỉ là Luật Jante (Janteloven). Khái niệm này bắt nguồn từ tiểu thuyết En flyktning krysser sitt spor xuất bản năm 1933 của nhà văn Đan Mạch - Na Uy Aksel Sandemose.
Luật này không tồn tại trong bất kỳ văn bản pháp luật nào nhưng nó đã thấm sâu vào văn hóa Bắc Âu đến mức trở thành một rào cản kinh doanh hữu hình đối với ngành hàng xa xỉ.
Nguyên tắc cốt lõi của nó khá đơn giản: người ta thường tránh thể hiện mình nổi bật hơn người khác, hạn chế khoe khoang thành tích và đặc biệt là không xem việc phô bày sự giàu có như một cách khẳng định địa vị.
Trong khuôn khổ văn hóa đó, việc trưng ra những món đồ đắt tiền không tự động mang lại sự ngưỡng mộ; thay vào đó, nó thường bị đọc là một nỗ lực khẳng định vị thế xã hội cao hơn, đi ngược lại với chuẩn mực bình đẳng mà xã hội Bắc Âu đề cao.
Điều quan trọng là họ không hề ghét vàng, họ vẫn sở hữu vàng như một tài sản đầu tư, một vật kỷ niệm gia đình nhưng họ giữ kín nó cho riêng mình, không bao giờ diện ra nơi công cộng.
Đối với các thương hiệu xa xỉ, đây là một thách thức chiến lược: không thể định vị đẳng cấp thương hiệu thông qua việc khuyến khích khách hàng phô trương.
Thông điệp “hãy thể hiện đẳng cấp của bạn” vốn phát huy hiệu quả tại Trung Đông, Ấn Độ hay Mỹ nhưng sẽ không phù hợp và có thể gây phản ứng ngược tại Bắc Âu.
Các thương hiệu thành công trong khu vực này như Ole Lynggaard của Đan Mạch hiểu biết rõ điều này.
Họ không bán sự lấp lánh. Cái họ bán là "sự thanh lịch kín đáo", kiểu giá trị đến từ tay nghề thủ công và ý nghĩa thiết kế, chứ không phải từ lượng vàng hay vẻ hào nhoáng bề ngoài.
Theo News18, Asianet Newsable, BBC Worklife, E24

articles.title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production in mid-2027 to build Cybercabs
articles.text:
Tesla will stop making most Cybertrucks at its Texas factory around the middle of next year, chief executive Elon Musk said on Friday. The space will instead be used to build more Cybercabs, the company’s two-seat robotaxis.
Musk announced the plan in a post on X, but he did not say whether production would end completely.
Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 6, 2026
Gigafactory Texas is the only plant that builds the Cybertruck. Tesla has not said what will happen to parts and servicing for existing owners. The truck has sold far below Tesla’s early hopes.
In 2023, Musk said Tesla could eventually sell 250,000 to 500,000 a year. However, the company has sold only tens of thousands in total since deliveries began in late 2023.
Tesla does not report Cybertruck sales on their own. Instead, it groups them with the Model S, Model X, and Semi, and that category fell 48% from a year earlier to 8,295 vehicles in the third quarter.
Based on those figures, Electrek estimates Tesla has delivered about 70,000 Cybertrucks in three years. The truck also missed the goals Tesla set when it was unveiled in 2019.
Also, the company promised a price under $40,000 and a range of up to 500 miles, but the truck arrived two years late, at about $60,000 and with a shorter range. Today the cheapest version starts at $74,990, after a $5,000 price rise in August.
Its divisive design and high price weighed on sales. Musk’s political activity in 2024 and 2025 also made the truck a target for protests, TechCrunch reported.
The Cybertruck is the latest product Tesla has dropped as it puts more money into AI and robotics. Earlier this year, it ended production of the Model S and Model X and used that space to build Optimus humanoid robots.
Meanwhile, Cybercab has been carrying passengers in Austin for about two months. Tesla plans to expand the service to Dallas later this month.

articles.title: Amazon is now making a Melania Trump TV series
articles.text:
Following the Melania documentary movie that premiered earlier this year, Amazon is now planning to release a two-part Prime Video series focusing on the first lady. The show, Melania: The Series, is set to debut on November 20th.
Amazon is now making a Melania Trump TV series
Melania Trump is the focus of a new two-part Prime Video show debuting later this month.
“MELANIA, The Series reveals never-before-told stories, offering unprecedented insight into Melania Trump’s life, including the extraordinary days immediately following the 47th Presidential Inauguration,” according to a description in a press release.

articles.title: Airbnb can buy into Chesky’s AI lab as revenue grows 19%
articles.text:
Brian Chesky’s AI lab paid Airbnb $7.1M for some of its intellectual property and to cover certain expenses, Airbnb disclosed in its quarterly filing on Thursday. Chesky, Airbnb’s chief executive, founded the lab and controls it.
Under the deal, signed this month, Airbnb can choose to join the lab’s future funding rounds. It also gets a licence to use some of the lab’s technology inside its own business. Chief technology officer Ahmad Al-Dahle holds a stake in the lab and works for it too. The Information, which reported the disclosure, said Chesky has funded the lab himself so far, citing a source. TNW has not independently verified that.
“Their roles with the AI Lab do not change their duties and responsibilities to Airbnb,” the filing said of the two executives.
A special committee of independent board members approved the deal under Airbnb’s policy on related-party transactions. The filing does not name the lab or say what it is building.
Al-Dahle joined Airbnb in January from Meta, where he led generative AI, Bloomberg reported at the time. We reported in June that Chesky was building an AI lab of his own.
Back in growth mode
The filing came with Airbnb’s third-quarter results. Revenue rose 19% to $4.9bn, its fastest growth in more than three years, and net income reached $1.9bn. Nights and seats booked rose 16%. Airbnb now expects revenue to grow in the high teens this year, up from at least the mid-teens. It also approved up to $12bn more in share buybacks.
“It’s rare for a marketplace of our size to reaccelerate growth, but that’s exactly what we’re doing,” Chesky told analysts on Thursday’s earnings call.
Airbnb last raised its forecast in August. Hotels, which it began adding this year, grew “markedly faster” than homes in the quarter, Chesky said.
Shares jumped more than 10% on Friday, Reuters reported. That set Airbnb apart from Booking, Expedia and Tripadvisor. All three have pointed to higher airfares linked to the Iran war and to unrest in parts of Europe, Reuters said.
Its own travel agent
Airbnb plans to start rolling out its own AI agent for planning and booking trips in the first half of 2027, it said alongside the results. Instead of a chat window, the agent will build each answer from maps, photos, comparisons, calendars and itineraries. It will also handle changes, refunds and payment problems after a booking.
Chesky argued that general assistants such as Meta’s Muse and Instinct are not built for travel. They still send Airbnb little business, he said on the call, as Business Insider reported.
“We’re not seeing a lot of traffic, and even fewer bookings, from Muse and Instinct yet,” Chesky said.
Agent traffic peaked in early October and has not grown since, he added. Airbnb’s own support assistant now resolves about 40% of customer issues without a human. Support costs per booking fell more than 17% from a year earlier, the company said.

articles.title: Paris start-up Physicl raises $10M to make training data for physical AI
articles.text:
Physicl, a Paris-based start-up that creates training data for AI systems that work in the physical world, has raised $10M in seed funding. Inovia Capital led the round, announced on Friday, with U.S. Venture Partners also taking part.
The company focuses on what researchers call edge cases. These are the unusual situations, such as odd lighting or an unexpected object in the way, where AI models for robots, self-driving cars, and 3D vision often make mistakes.
Its first product, Studio, lets researchers rebuild those situations in 3D. They pick an environment or describe a scene where their model struggles, then change the lighting, the camera angle, and where objects sit.
Studio then produces accurate training data aimed at that specific weakness. As a result, researchers can recreate a failure, test a fix, and measure whether their model has improved.
The platform includes 10,000 3D environments and more than 100,000 objects, which can be combined into billions of different scenes, according to the company.
“Models fail on edge cases. When researchers find these weaknesses, they need a way to generate data that specifically addresses them,” said Alex de Vigan, Physicl’s founder and chief executive.
De Vigan previously founded Nfinite, a Paris company that makes 3D images of products for online retailers and raised $100m in 2022. He has spent six years working on 3D, simulation, and machine learning.
Physicl already works with AI labs and universities, including Meta, World Labs, Epic Games, Amazon Web Services, Nvidia, and the Technical University of Munich.
One customer is SpAItial, a Munich start-up that builds 3D AI models. After adding Physicl’s data to its training set, SpAItial cut the error rate of its room-building model by more than half, the company said.
Physicl will use the capital to grow its team and develop the platform further. It joins a wave of European start-ups working on physical AI, the technology that lets machines understand and act in the real world.

articles.title: Just about anyone can rent access to White House IP addresses
articles.text:
Someone at the White House appears to be running software that could enable outsiders to rent access on the presidential network for just “a few dollars,” as reported by Krebs on Security and The Register. That’s according to findings from the security firms Layer3 Intel and Synthient, which discovered residential proxy activity on the White House network.
Just about anyone can rent access to White House IP addresses
Security researchers discovered residential proxy activity on the White House’s network.
A residential proxy opens up a way for people to rent access to a home IP address and route their internet traffic through it, allowing them to conceal where their activity is actually coming from. Some apps and browser extensions include third-party software development kits (SDKs) that put proxy nodes on a user’s device — whether users know it or not. Third-party services can then sell access to the residential proxies on users’ devices.
As noted by the cybersecurity firm Spur, people can legitimately use residential proxies for purposes like ad verification and quality assurance testing, but bad actors can also use them to bypass geolocation controls and defensive filters. Hackers have used residential proxies for all kinds of malicious activity, including to create botnets and carry out account takeovers.
At the White House, Layer3 Intel found that 28 residential proxy services routed traffic out of the network from October 5th to November 3rd. It notes that this activity typically happens between 5PM ET and midnight. “That pattern suggests a person rather than a public guest Wi-Fi network: someone regularly on the White House network late into the evening, whose device is infected with a proxy SDK,” Layer3 says. The SDK in question might be linked to the watch party app Rave, according to Synthient, which says the app “bundles 12 proxy SDKs into the platform.”
Synthient found “a number of Windows 10 and Windows 11 devices on the White House’s network beaconing to known proxy providers like Geonode, Infatica and Mellowtel.” As noted by Krebs on Security, Infatica is a proxy service founded by Vladimir Fomenko, the owner of King Servers, which was linked to 2016 cyberattacks on election systems in Illinois and Arizona.
Layer3 warns that the residential proxy is “public access,” adding that “anybody can obtain it by signing up to a public residential proxy service, paying a few dollars and sending requests through it.”

articles.title: Cramer’s week ahead: AI data center stocks face another hurdle and so does the Fed
articles.text:
CNBC's Jim Cramer on Friday said that next week's earnings from leading neoclouds could test investor confidence in the battered data center trade.
Stocks rebounded to end a turbulent election week, which saw investors dumping companies tied to the artificial intelligence infrastructure build-out after Democrats flipped the House and Senate and some key gubernatorial seats. Following the worst day on Wall Street in 19 months, Friday's gains were welcome but not to be trusted. Cramer remained skeptical of any recovery, as he also had been about what proved to be Wednesday's short-lived midterm rally.
Cramer argued that concerns about data center spending and financing have yet to be resolved. "It felt like a dead cat bounce," the "Mad Money" host said, referring to Friday's largely positive market. "I know we are never going to get an all clear. But it still feels like there are plenty of sellers lurking, just waiting for stocks to make a bigger recovery so they can get out."
With that backdrop, Cramer turned to the week ahead.
Monday
Constellation Energy reports before the bell, offering an early look at how political uncertainty could affect the power infrastructure supporting AI data centers.
Tuesday
On Holding reports earnings, but Cramer remains cautious on the athletic footwear. He said the industry feels increasingly crowded. "I am going to pass on this one," he said.
The consumer price index also arrives Tuesday morning, with Cramer looking for a meaningful slowdown in inflation. He warned that persistently high prices could prompt Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh to raise interest rates again. The Fed hiked rates in September for the first time in three years.
After the close, neocloud CoreWeave reports in what could be one of the week's most consequential earnings releases. Cramer said the heavily indebted neocloud needs to explain how it plans to finance its expansion and manage its borrowing costs.
Wednesday
Corteva reports in an otherwise quiet session. Cramer said the agricultural chemicals company has fallen sharply out of favor with investors and wants to better understand what's weighing on its stock.
Thursday
Nebius, another high-profile neocloud, reports before the bell, providing another major test for the AI infrastructure trade following results from CoreWeave. Cramer said investors will be looking for strong new orders, completed data centers and a robust pipeline of future projects. "What I don't want to hear is that the sites they are building are coming in late and overbudget," he said.
Cisco Systems also reports Thursday evening. He said the networking provider may be oversold, but would wait to see how the market responds to CoreWeave and Nebius before buying.
Applied Materials reports as well. Although the semiconductor equipment maker's shares have fallen sharply from their highs, Cramer cautioned that a steep decline alone does not make a stock attractive. "Remember, we don't care where a stock comes from. We just care about where it is going," he said.
Kraft Heinz holds an investor meeting Thursday. Cramer remains optimistic about CEO Steve Cahillane's ability to unlock shareholder value, citing his track record at Kellogg.
Friday
The producer price index comes in Friday, offering another important reading on inflation.

articles.title: SpaceX says Google exec Don Harrison has resigned from its board
articles.text:
SpaceX said on Friday that longtime Google executive Donald Harrison has resigned from the rocket maker's board of directors.
Harrison has worked at Google since 2005, and is the search giant's president of global partnerships and corporate development. In a regulatory filing, SpaceX said "Mr. Harrison's decision to resign was not due to any disagreement with the Company on any matter relating to its operations, policies, or practices."
SpaceX thanked Harrison for his "many contributions and his years of dedicated and outstanding service" to the company.
The announcement comes roughly five months after SpaceX went public in the largest IPO on record. Google parent Alphabet maintains close ties with SpaceX, having invested in Elon Musk's company in 2015, when it was valued at about $12 billion.
Alphabet is now the largest institutional investor n SpaceX, with a stake worth $74 billion as of Friday's close. SpaceX's current market cap is about $1.8 trillion.
Google is a key customer of SpaceX, and has agreed to pay the company's AI division up to $920 million a month for compute capacity from its data centers in the area around Memphis, Tennessee. The companies also recently worked together to launch Google AI chips into orbit via Project Suncatcher.
"While Don is stepping down from the board, we remain deeply supportive of SpaceX's mission and are excited to continue our long-standing partnership," Google said in an emailed statement.

articles.title: Investors brace for lower Anthropic valuation, calling $1.5 trillion a 'stretch'
articles.text:
Following tech's selloff on Wall Street this week, some investors are lowering their expectations for Anthropic.
The artificial intelligence company had been looking toward a $2 trillion valuation in its IPO up until recently, but stakeholders told CNBC that even $1.5 trillion is now in doubt, with one investor calling that number a "stretch."
Anthropic declined to comment.
The change in sentiment comes alongside growing concerns about the outsized spending by AI companies and a sharp post-midterm slump in the market. The Nasdaq plummeted more than 5% on Thursday, its steepest drop in 19 months, reflecting fears that Democrats' newfound power in Washington, D.C., and a nationwide rebuke of AI will lead to a slowdown in the buildout of data centers.
Bearishness on the AI trade was on the rise before the election. The Nasdaq suffered its worst month in October since March 2025, led by declines in chipmakers and neoclouds.
Anthropic is set to list on the Nasdaq, under the ticker ANT, and is gearing up for an expected debut in a matter of weeks. Last month, Anthropic was reportedly seeking a valuation as high as $2 trillion. As of May, the company was privately valued at $965 billion.
With the latest market turmoil, one investor said $1 trillion to $1.25 trillion is a more likely valuation target, although that could change with market conditions. The investors asked not to be named because they're not authorized to speak about the matter.
Gil Luria, an analyst at D.A. Davidson, told CNBC that, "Investors will expect the IPO to be priced at least at the low end of previous expectations."
"The market really needs this IPO to go well and the bankers on the deal surely understand that," Luria said. "The best way to set Anthropic up for success is to price the deal well."
The company is expected to kick off its roadshow next week.
WATCH: Some Anthropic investors now skeptical of $1.5 trillion valuation

articles.title: Sen. Chris Murphy released from hospital after stroke, will miss votes for 'several weeks' as he rehabs
articles.text:
Connecticut Democratic Sen. Chris Murphy said Friday he had been released from a hospital after suffering a stroke last weekend.
Murphy, 53, said he will be in a rehabilitation center for the next "several weeks," meaning he will miss votes in the Senate when Congress returns on Monday.
"The doctors are very encouraged by the progress I've made so far," he said in a statement.
"In order to take my recovery seriously and get back to work on the quickest timeline possible, I will be spending several weeks at a rehabilitation center after being discharged from the hospital today," said Murphy, who has been discussed as a possible presidential candidate in 2028.
Dr. Jose Suarez, chief of Neurosciences Critical Care at The Johns Hopkins Hospital, in a statement released by Murphy's office, said, "Senator Murphy experienced a small hemorrhagic stroke."
"He has shown tremendous progress, and at the current rate of improvement, we expect that he will make a full recovery following rehabilitation," Suarez said.
Murphy had been in the hospital since having a stroke at his son's hockey game.
"Last Saturday afternoon, I felt something was not right with my body and called 9-1-1 out of an abundance of caution, and I'm glad I did," Murphy said in his statement. "I was diagnosed with a small bleed in the thalamus region of my brain."
The senator said he was grateful "for the outpouring of support my family and I have received over the last few days."
"This has been a scary experience for me and my family, and I appreciate the continued respect for our privacy," Murphy said. "As I'm working towards a full recovery, I am staying engaged with my team and colleagues remotely, and my staff continues to carry out our legislative priorities, serve constituents, and ensure the work of my office continues uninterrupted."
Murphy's stroke came three days before Democratic candidates, in a stunning election result, won more than enough races to flip the Senate and House of Representatives from Republican majority control in January.
Murphy, who was not up for reelection this year, before the election had campaigned for Democratic candidates around the country, most recently in Michigan, Minnesota and Florida. He had been scheduled to campaign in New Hampshire on Sunday with Rep. Chris Pappas, who on Tuesday won election to the Senate.

articles.title: Here's a rapid-fire update on all 31 of our stocks, including 2 to buy now
articles.text: Jim Cramer and portfolio director Jeff Marks closed out a wild market week on Friday at the Investing Club's fourth Annual Meeting at the New York Stock Exchange. They reviewed all 31 stocks in the Club's portfolio in the wake of Tuesday's election, which has cast doubt on the future of the artificial intelligence buildout. Jim made it clear that he believes there could be more turbulence ahead for AI stocks, but he also sees non-tech opportunities for those with cash on hand. FedEx and Kimberly-Clark are the names he recommended buying here. He said to wait for more selling in Johnson & Johnson and Eli Lilly before scooping up shares. Here's our stock-by-stock review of the entire Investing Club portfolio: Apple : We view Apple as an "own it, don't trade it" stock. The iPhone maker has a major advantage in the AI race because it can leverage the technology of its partner, Alphabet, without spending billions building its own data centers. Easing tariffs and a potential peak in memory prices could provide additional upside. Amazon : Investors overlooked the strength of its latest quarter, particularly the growth in its cloud unit, AWS. Unlike some hyperscalers, Amazon builds its own data centers rather than relying on heavily indebted neocloud providers, giving it greater control over its AI expansion. Boeing : We bought the post-earnings sell-off and would like to add more. Although the planemaker pushed back its $10 billion free cash flow target by roughly a year, we remain confident in CEO Kelly Ortberg's turnaround efforts. Lower oil prices and resilient travel demand should support aircraft orders, making the recent weakness an opportunity. Bank of New York : CEO Robin Vince's turnaround continues to deliver stronger profitability and operating efficiency. With limited credit risk and an attractive valuation, we see BNY as a compelling way to diversify the portfolio away from technology while maintaining exposure to a high-quality financial company. Cardinal Health : We trimmed our position following another excellent quarter to avoid giving back substantial gains. The pharmaceutical distributor continues to execute exceptionally well, particularly in its specialty business, but the stock's nearly vertical rally warranted taking some profits. Capital One : Despite the credit card company's inexpensive valuation and healthy credit metrics, investors are concerned that Democrats could renew efforts to cap credit card interest rates following their midterm victories. However, it's unlikely the proposal would become law, as previous attempts have not resulted in anything material. So, we hold on, while being mindful of the headline risk. Costco : The wholesaler's improving sales trends and stabilizing membership renewal rates reinforce our confidence in Costco. Management appears to be refocusing on the company's core strategy of delivering exceptional value and driving sales volume. Though shares aren't cheap at roughly 46 times earnings, we prefer Costco over Walmart . Salesforce : We remain confident in Salesforce as it partners with leading AI labs, most notably Anthropic, to integrate its software applications into their platforms. These partnerships reinforce our belief that Salesforce can benefit from AI rather than be disrupted by it. CrowdStrike : As artificial intelligence makes cybersecurity threats more dangerous, CrowdStrike stands to be one of the biggest beneficiaries. We remain bullish, but have periodically trimmed to rightsize its weighting in the portfolio. DuPont : We sold some shares of the supplier of industrial materials ahead of earnings, but remain encouraged by CEO Lori Koch's execution following the Qnity spin-off. Its healthcare, water and industrial businesses provide exposure to attractive non-AI areas, while construction-related demand has held up better than expected. Eaton : The electrical equipment supplier remains an excellent company, but its exposure to data center construction makes it vulnerable to a slowdown in AI spending. With both Eaton and GE Vernova in the portfolio, we may need to trim one to reduce our overall exposure to the buildout. FedEx : This is a stock to buy right here. CEO Raj Subramaniam continues to cut costs and prioritize higher-value shipments, while new warehouse robotics could further improve efficiency. With management optimistic about the holiday season and oil prices potentially declining, FedEx can continue taking share from rival UPS. FedEx Freight : We still like the less-than-truckload shipping company following last week's strong quarter, which demonstrated the benefits of operating independently. However, FedEx's remaining 20% stake creates an overhang that may be keeping large institutional investors on the sidelines. We'd prefer to wait until that block of shares is sold before making a more substantial purchase. GE Vernova : We still believe in GE Vernova's long-term growth prospects, supported by strong turbine demand, grid modernization and a backlog extending into the early 2030s. But, as mentioned with Eaton, we're weighing whether to reduce exposure to AI industrials as investors sour on the broader data center trade. Alphabet : Although Google Cloud continues to deliver exceptional growth, we're concerned that Gemini could increasingly cannibalize Google's core search business. The company's decision to issue shares rather than repurchase them also dents our confidence, making Alphabet our least favorite of the major hyperscalers. Goldman Sachs : We added to our position on Thursday and would be happy to buy more. At roughly 12 times earnings, the stock looks inexpensive given its strong investment banking and trading businesses, which should benefit from heightened market volatility. Goldman is also a lead underwriter on Anthropic's planned IPO, which could be another potential catalyst if the offering helps restore confidence in the AI trade. Home Depot : Our thesis hasn't entirely gone according to plan, as housing market activity remains subdued. But shares have performed much better since early October as bond yields retreated, underscoring why we've stayed patient and the importance of diversification. Intel : This position has become a terrible mistake after the chipmaker issued disappointing guidance last week. No way around it. Jim apologized for not fully recognizing how the CPU renaissance could be derailed by a PC slowdown and a factory fire. Management will need to rebuild credibility. Johnson & Johnson : The drugmaker and medical technology giant has been a terrific winner for us since we switched out of Bristol Myers Squibb this spring. J & J has a robust drug pipeline, and one of its existing cancer drugs just secured expanded approval from the FDA. Kimberly-Clark : The Huggies parent reported better-than-feared third-quarter results on Thursday, and the closure of the Kenvue acquisition on Monday is a big milestone. We're optimistic that CEO Michael Hsu will improve operations at the owner of Tylenol and Neutrogena. Plus, Kimberly pays a nice dividend. Jim said that if you wanted to build a 100-share position, buy 25 shares right now. Eli Lilly : A longtime holding for us, Lilly has the leading injectable GLP-1s and an impressive pipeline of next-generation assets in its pipeline. We trimmed some Thursday out of discipline. But if there's another sell-off in Lilly, this would be a name to buy. Linde : This is another long-term stalwart in the portfolio. It's had a nice gain this year, benefiting from supplying gases to semiconductor manufacturers. The one blemish is its home healthcare unit, known as Lincare. However, the company has taken the problem seriously, reinforcing our trust in senior leadership. Meta Platforms : We must stay mindful of Meta's plans to commence an at-the-money stock offering next year. Though shares have been hit in the AI sell-off, that has made us feel better about our trim in September during the height of the Muse agent excitement. This name can rise over time. Microsoft : The rare hyperscaler that's remained free cash flow positive, Microsoft has righted the ship in a remarkable way over the past two quarterly reports. CFO Amy Hood is a disciplined executive. It's become a must-own. Micron : We're not in a hurry to add to our position given the uncertainty around the AI trade right now. The potential start of a monster buyback program in December is a promising catalyst. We do regret not peeling off any stock into its big run from September into early October. Nvidia : Speaking of large buybacks, Nvidia has a more than $200 billion authorization, and we want to see the chipmaker deploy it aggressively and routinely be in the market offering support when shares are under pressure. We're not deviating from our "own it, don't trade it" mantra. Palo Alto Networks : Similar thesis to fellow cybersecurity vendor CrowdStrike. One thing with Palo Alto that really shines is CEO Nikesh Arora's track record of making smart acquisitions before the target company's business really inflects. CyberArk in the identity security space is a recent example of this. Qnity Electronics : The semiconductor materials supplier reported an excellent beat-and-raise quarter earlier this week. In such a fraught moment for AI names, the market didn't give Qnity any credit. Though off its year-highs, we're not putting Qnity in the troubled camp. It benefits more from the rise in chip volumes than from price. Starbucks : CEO Brian Niccol has the coffee chain firing on all cylinders and outperforming competitors. Starbucks' decision to not raise prices to keep up with inflation helped win customers. Now, margins are starting to improve. TJX Companies : Last quarter was shocking — and not in a good way —as its most important reporting segment—home to T.J. Maxx and Marshalls—disappointed. So far, we've been rewarded for buying the dip. Need to see an improvement in the upcoming quarter to restore our faith in the off-price retailer we've loved for years for its reliability. Wells Fargo : The asset cap is gone, and we're looking for a strong 2027. Shares look cheap, and CEO Charlie Scharf has straightened out the company and invested in building out an investment bank and other fee-based businesses. We take a longer-term view with this one. articles.title: Further turmoil could be in store for tech stocks. What to watch in the week ahead
articles.text: This latest bout of market turbulence may still get worse before it gets better. Investors wrapped up a topsy-turvy week in markets. After the Dow Jones Industrial Average soared 1,500 points on Wednesday, the day after the U.S. midterm elections, it promptly erased all those gains on Thursday, plunging 1,800 points in the worst sell-off Wall Street had seen since April 2025 — which was when President Donald Trump announced his so-called "liberation day" tariffs. That's not all: The Nasdaq Composite plunged into a correction, as artificial intelligence stocks bore the brunt of the selling. The single-day pillaging left the Magnificent Seven companies collectively poorer by $1 trillion , with Nvidia alone suddenly out a stunning $440 billion. Stocks recouped some of those losses on Friday, but traders don't expect the bleeding is over just yet — even if they start taking a bite here and there, especially in semiconductors. "What I look for is this to continue over the next few days, maybe another week, before we hit a bottom," said Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets. No panic yet Even before a Democratic sweep of the House and Senate complicated the outlook for data center development in the U.S., investors had been anxiously waiting for the stock market to press the reset button on the AI trade. In many ways, the stock market has managed to avoid a true capitulation thus far thanks to a buy-the-dip mentality that has kept retail traders circulating their cash through the different parts of the market without ever leaving. More recently, they've been piling into defensive sectors such as healthcare and consumer staples, making even the safety trades look overbought. Meanwhile, the S & P 500, in spite of its many fits and starts this fall, is essentially where it was in July. .SPX YTD mountain S & P 500, YTD Now the market looks closer to finding a durable bottom. Thursday marked the biggest day of retail selling since the Covid pandemic, according to Vanda Research, as individual investors joined their institutional counterparts in pulling back from the market. But the losses aren't severe enough yet. Bob Lang, chief options analyst at Explosive Options, said he needs to see several days of selling before calling a bottom. He noted that the CBOE put/call ratio on Thursday rose to 1.2, double the average at 0.6, which indicates 1.2 puts being bought for every call. It's an extreme level of bearishness that's often a contrarian signal to buy stocks. But, he said he would need more readings just like that one after this week's ugly drawdown. Freedom Capital Markets' Woods said he's watching the CBOE Volatility Index , otherwise known as Wall Street's fear gauge, which he would need to see climb above 30 before he can say there's a real flush. On Friday, it was last at around the 24 handle. "We're very close to this final capitulation," Woods said. "We're not seeing the panic yet, but we are seeing opportunities." Drawing up shopping lists Woods thinks the highs may be in for the year, as there's little left on the calendar that could serve as a durable positive catalyst for the market. The S & P 500 climbed to record highs just last month, topping 7,800. The third-quarter earnings season, which proved to be as impressive as anticipated, is largely behind traders, even with some big names like Nvidia still to come later this month. By the time it wraps up, the S & P 500 is expected to have grown earnings by 31% last quarter, according to FactSet's John Butters. The results confirm yet again the unprecedented heft American companies are enjoying thanks to AI, gains that are expanding to the 493 companies outside of the Magnificent Seven. Washington will remain in focus, as investors await how a divided government tackles spending on the Iran war, a battle that could result in a government shutdown before the year is out. The path for monetary policy remains in focus, especially after Friday's blowout payrolls report showed that hourly wages continue to grow and implied that the job market is holding up. Investors will get more clarity on the inflation front in the coming week, with the releases of both the consumer and producer price indexes. According to early estimates averaged on FactSet, CPI is expected to have increased 3.9% on a year over year basis, worse than the 3.7% in the prior reading, but core inflation is set to have cooled somewhat on a monthly basis. Some investors are drawing up their shopping lists to go bargain hunting following this week's rout. Freedom Capital Markets' Woods said he spies opportunities in Micron and Nvidia, both of which have been heavily punished in the recent sell-off, as well as the broader semiconductor space. "It's not the time to jump in with both feet," Woods said. "But it's time to start nibbling because to pick that bottom will be very difficult." Week ahead calendar All times ET.
